extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent applicants, and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how the USPTO applies the 2019 Revised Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance (2019 PEG), including how examiners should identify abstract ideas, groupings, tentative abstract ideas, integration into practical application, and provide notice for eligibility rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of the October 2019 Update
rubrics_metrics.description: The update does not change the 2019 PEG, but provides further explanation on how the USPTO applies such guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the October 2019 materials as explanatory clarification of the 2019 PEG rather than a substantive change to the underlying guidance. Use the update to understand application practices but not as a change in policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining if a claim 'recites' an abstract idea
rubrics_metrics.description: The update provides additional information on how the USPTO determines if a claim 'recites' an abstract idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the explanations and examples in the update to assess whether claim language recites subject matter that falls within an abstract idea; follow the USPTO's procedures and illustrative examples to inform the factual and legal analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: How groupings within the abstract idea exception are determined
rubrics_metrics.description: The update provides additional information on how groupings within the abstract idea exception are determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the USPTO's approach to categorize abstract ideas into appropriate groupings when analyzing claims, using the update's explanations to choose consistent groupings for examination and reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures to identify 'tentative abstract ideas'
rubrics_metrics.description: The update explains the procedures examiners can use to identify 'tentative abstract ideas'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should follow the described procedures to form and document tentative determinations about abstract-idea character, refining those determinations with claim context and examples before issuing a final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating integration of a judicial exception into a practical application
rubrics_metrics.description: The update provides more information on how examiners evaluate whether a judicial exception is integrated into a practical application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the update's tests and examples to determine whether claim limitations integrate a judicial exception into a practical application (i.e., whether the claim as a whole applies, uses, or improves a technology or technical field).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner responsibility to provide adequate notice for subject matter eligibility rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The update addresses the examiner’s responsibility to provide adequate notice to applicants in making a subject matter eligibility rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When issuing an eligibility rejection, examiners must give clear, adequate notice explaining the basis for the rejection (including how the claim is characterized and which judicial exception is implicated) so applicants can respond meaningfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of additional examples in life sciences and data processing
rubrics_metrics.description: The update includes additional helpful examples in the life sciences and data processing areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to these sector-specific examples to see how the 2019 PEG applies in life sciences and data processing contexts; use them as illustrative precedent for claim analysis and examiner training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated index of examples for use with the 2019 PEG
rubrics_metrics.description: The update includes an updated index of examples for use with the 2019 PEG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the updated index to locate relevant illustrative examples when applying the 2019 PEG to particular claim types or technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated case law chart of selected eligibility cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The update includes an updated case law chart that lists selected eligibility cases from the U.S. Supreme Court and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the updated chart to identify and reference key judicial decisions relevant to subject matter eligibility analyses; the chart aids in aligning examiner practice with controlling and persuasive case law.
